Users in Europe wanted lower latency. We deployed to eu-west-1, pointed DNS at both regions, and called it multi-region.

Within a week: duplicate order IDs, conflicting profile updates, and a cart that looked like it belonged to someone else. Reads got faster. Correctness got harder.

Multi-region is not "run the same stack twice." It's a choice between:

• Active-passive — one write primary, DR region on standby. Simpler consistency.
• Active-active — both regions take writes. You need a conflict strategy before you flip the switch.

Replication lag is physics. A user who writes in the US and reads from EU may not see their update until you design for that (sticky region, read-after-write, version checks).

CDN + read replicas solve a lot of global latency without active-active writes. Active-active is the heavy option — not the default.
